note: Medieval Benedictine nunnery, later a castle, beside Ringsjön in Höör, with church, gardens and park.
Twelfth-century sandstone church of the former nunnery, standing beside Bosjökloster castle.
Bronze Age rock carving in Boglösa, Enköping, of a ship more than four metres long with six paddlers.
Preserved iron blast furnace at the former Brattfors ironworks in Filipstad, closed in 1920.
Eighteenth-century post windmill at Broa on Fårö, given to Bunge museum in 1936 and kept open.
Viking Age bridge site at Broby in Täby, with several Jarlabanke runestones standing by the road.
Single lock on Kinda kanal at Brokind, linking Lilla Rängen and Järnlunden beside Brokind castle.
Bronze Age ship settings at Gnisvärd in Tofta on Gotland, the largest about 47 metres long.
Long dry-stone wall at Kaspersbo by Garpenberg, said to have been built to work off liquor debts.
Single lock on the Östergötland stretch of Göta kanal, earlier spelled Brådtom and first named Stockholm.
Viking Age runestone Sö 292, called Brötastenen, standing near Bröta in Grödinge, Botkyrka.
Sealed coastal bunker, number 683, on the Per Albin Line along the shore in northwestern Skåne.
Sealed machine-gun bunker, number 687, on the Per Albin Line a short walk from bunker 683.
Small Second World War bunker on eastern Gotland that visitors can climb into, with a view of the sea.
Small three-room bunker in a park in Uppsala, near Husargatan, now open after having been sealed.
Small lock station on Dalslands kanal at Buterud, between Håverud and the lakes to the north.
Old mill and salmon ladder at the former Böksholm ironworks on Mörrumsån near Braås.
Ruin of the medieval parish church at Börringe, abandoned when a new church was built in the 1780s.

note: Lock staircase at Berg on Göta kanal, whose Carl Johan flight of seven locks is part of eleven locks in all.
Surviving seventeenth-century bastion of Gothenburg's fortifications at Kungshöjd, called Carolus XI Rex.
Manor south of Gamleby on Gamlebyviken, rebuilt in 1829 on an older estate of the Lewenhaupt family.
Dutch-style windmill from 1851 southwest of Malmöhus, the last mill inside Malmö's canals.
Cementa's limestone quarry at Albrunna on southern Öland, a flooded pit used by birds and swimmers.
Surviving stretch of Lund's medieval earth rampart and moat, now a path through Stadsparken.
Small rock cave by Dackestupet at Virserumssjön, where legend says the wounded Nils Dacke was hidden in 1543.
Memorial stone in the woods at Rabbe, south of Ledja in Blekinge, at the place where Nils Dacke is said to have been killed.
Former execution mound at the southeast edge of Dalby, used for public executions into the nineteenth century.
Water mill from 1893 on Dalens ström at Koberg in Lagmansered, cared for by the local heritage association.
Medieval gate in Visby's town wall at Östergravar, about 17 metres high and later used as a granary.
Flooded medieval iron mine on a point in Dalmyrasjön on Vikbolandet, now a picnic place reached by a raft.
Remote lock on Dalslands kanal, with an opening railway bridge and rapids, south of Bengtsfors.
Lock station on Dalslands kanal in Dals Långed, built when the canal was cut through the village in the 1860s.
One of the five heavy forts of Boden Fortress, on Degerberget, in service from 1908 until 1992 and now fenced off.
Outdoor remains of the ironworks and later pulp mill at Delary on Helge å, west of Älmhult.
Norwegian gift stone outside Helsingborg city hall, thanking Sweden for bringing home prisoners in 1945.
Director's house at Sala silver mine, built in the 1820s as a clerk's dwelling and enlarged for the mine director in the 1880s.
Cluster of glacial potholes in the cliff above Magelungen at Djupån in Ågesta, Huddinge.
A site called Domarringen near Falun that visitors describe as unsigned and hard to find.
Viking Age runestone DR 262 at Fosie church in Malmö, raised by Asbjörn in memory of Dvärg.
Kettle hole left by the retreating ice sheet in the Drakamöllan nature reserve in eastern Skåne.
Small monument on the island of Hanö, linked to a legend of a dragon that fled the lighthouse.
Half-timbered house on Otterhällan in Gothenburg, documented from the 1730s and moved to Otterhällegatan in 1972.
Uddnäs lock on Strömsholms kanal, named Drottning Sofia Magdalena, with a fall of about three metres.
Iron Age cemetery of standing stones and stone settings at Dörby beside Norra Möckleby on Öland.
Neolithic dolmen on Tjörn at Dösevägen, also called Valla dös or Styrdalen dös.
Two public fireplaces rebuilt by Botkyrka municipality in a nature reserve.
Bedrock cave on Högberget above Svensbyn, named for the nineteenth-century thief Elias Bäckman.
Coastal fort on Aspö outside Karlskrona, built in 1900–1904 and closed as a fixed fortification in 1959.
Former execution place at Endre on Gotland, called Endre backe, with little left above ground.
Closed Boliden gold mine at Enåsen near Ramsjö in Ljusdal, now a turquoise flooded pit.
